q: How much must a UK employer pay someone aged 21 or over, per hour, as of April 2026?
note: National Living Wage, 21 and over: £12.71. The rejects are the rates from earlier years, which is what a model recites from training data.

q: A UK worker is 19 years old and not an apprentice. What is the least their employer can lawfully pay them per hour?
note: 18 to 20 band: £10.85. Rejecting 12.71 too — answering with the 21-and-over rate is the specific error, not a harmless extra.

q: What is the UK minimum hourly wage for a 16 year old who has left school?
note: Under 18: £8. Without the rejects, '£8.60' scores as a pass because £8 is a substring of it.

q: What is the UK apprentice minimum wage hourly rate?
note: Apprentice rate: £8.

q: On what date do UK National Minimum Wage rates change each year?
note: 1 April. 6 April is the tax year and the most attractive wrong answer.

q: A UK apprentice is 22 and in the second year of their apprenticeship. What hourly rate are they legally entitled to?
note: The apprentice rate expires: 19+ and past the first year means the ordinary rate for their age, so £12.71.

q: Under what conditions is a UK apprentice entitled to the apprentice minimum wage rate rather than the rate for their age?
note: Either under 19, or 19+ and in the first year of the apprenticeship. Bare '19' removed: it matched any answer that mentioned the age at all, including one that got the condition backwards.

q: A UK worker turns 21 tomorrow. What is the minimum they must be paid per hour for the shift they work today?
note: Age on the day worked. Today they are still in the 18-to-20 band. No reject on 12.71 — a correct answer may well mention what they get tomorrow.

q: In the UK, does a worker's job title or seniority affect which National Minimum Wage band applies to them?
note: Bands are age brackets only. Graded on 'age' alone rather than on a negation: a wrong answer that says seniority matters will not name age as the determinant, and 'no'/'not' appear in almost any sentence.

q: At what age does a UK worker become entitled to the National Living Wage rather than a lower minimum wage band?
note: 21. It was 23 and before that 25, and those are exactly what a model trained on older data says. A bare two-digit marker is safe HERE only because the rejects carry the discrimination: an answer saying '23, reduced from 21' contains 21 but is killed by the reject.

q: How much Statutory Sick Pay does a UK employee get per week?
note: The lower of £123.25 and 80% of average weekly earnings. Both halves required — quoting the flat figure alone is the failure this pack exists to fix.

q: Is UK Statutory Sick Pay a flat weekly amount that every eligible employee receives?
note: It is the lower of the weekly rate and 80% of average weekly earnings. A wrong answer asserting a flat rate contains neither marker.

q: Over what period are average weekly earnings calculated for UK Statutory Sick Pay?
note: 8 weeks; employees with fewer than 8 weeks of earnings still qualify.

q: What is the maximum number of weeks a UK employer must pay Statutory Sick Pay for?
note: 28 weeks. Bare '28' is deliberate and safe here: the competing answers are other week counts, and each is rejected explicitly.

q: How many unpaid waiting days are there in the UK before Statutory Sick Pay begins?
note: None — SSP is paid from the first full working day of sickness. The old three-waiting-day rule is the confident wrong answer.

q: Which days of the week does UK Statutory Sick Pay actually get paid for?
note: Qualifying days = the days the employee normally works.

q: Name two situations in which a UK employee is not eligible for Statutory Sick Pay.
note: Already had the 28 weeks; receiving Statutory Maternity Pay.

q: After taking a tenancy deposit in England, how long does a landlord have to put it in a protection scheme?
note: 30 days from receiving it.

q: A tenant in England and their landlord have agreed how much of the deposit comes back. By when must the landlord actually return it?
note: 10 days from agreement. No reject on 30 days — a correct answer may contrast it with the protection deadline.

q: Which government-approved schemes can hold a tenancy deposit in England and Wales?
note: All three required — naming one of three is not an answer to 'which schemes'.

q: Besides protecting the money, what else must an England and Wales landlord do about a deposit, and within what time?
note: Give the tenant the prescribed information within the same 30 days. Two duties, one deadline.

q: Do the tenancy deposit protection rules and schemes for England and Wales also apply in Scotland?
note: Scotland and Northern Ireland run separate schemes. Scope discipline — the pack must not export an England and Wales rule.

q: Which kind of tenancy, and starting from what date, is covered by the England and Wales deposit protection rules?
note: Assured shorthold tenancies started after 6 April 2007.

q: The UK minimum wage rates I have are the April 2026 set. From when should I stop quoting them as current?
note: They are superseded on 1 April 2027. A statutory figure without a date stays confident after it expires.
